4. On his such statement, FIR was registered and investigation was conducted wherein it was revealed that appellant/accused was supposed to maintain the covers of manholes being supervisor appointed by the firm M/s A.K. Sharma Constructions as contracted by DDA.

26. Ld. counsel for the appellant has submitted that he is not challenging the judgment of the trial court on merits.
However, he prayed that in view of the fact that compensation amount has been received by the LRs of the deceased, appellant/accused be released on probation.
He also requested for some time to move the appropriate application.
27. On this, Ld. Counsel for the father of the deceased submitted that she has no objection if the appellant/accused is released on probation.

It has been contended by Ld. Counsel for the appellant that since the LRs of the victim have already received adequate compensation from DDA and in view of the fact that the offence u/s 304-A IPC prescribes the punishment not more than 2 years and further there is no history of previous conviction of the appellant, therefore, provisions of Section 3 of the Probation of Offenders Act are applied in the present case.

Ld. Counsel further contended that PRAVEEN PRAVEEN KUMAR KUMAR Date:

It has been contended that after payment of compensation to the victim, DDA is now persuading the remedy of recovery of such compensation from the appellant and upholding of conviction may strengthen the case of DDA to effect recovery of compensation so paid to the victim from the appellant.
It has, therefore, been prayed that appellant/accused be released on probation.
29. I have made my queries from prosecution as well.
Sh. V.K.Swami, Ld. Addl. PP for the State has also left it to this court to pass appropriate order in the aforesaid background.
30. I have given my thoughtful consideration to the contentions made by Ld. Counsel for the appellant.
I have also gone through the trial court record.
As the appellant is not challenging the judgment of trial court on merits, the same is upheld.

sentences.text:
Section 3 of Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 reads as under:-
PRAVEEN PRAVEEN KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.03.12 15:25:10 +0530 "3. Power of Court to release certain offenders after admonition - When any person is found guilty of having committed an offence punishable under section 379 or section 380 or section 381 or section 404 or section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) or any offence punishable with imprisonment for not more than two years, or with fine,
or with both, under the Indian Penal Code, or any other law, and no previous conviction is proved against him and the Court by which the person is found guilty is of opinion that, having regard to the circumstances of the case including the nature of the offence, and the character of the offender, it is expedient so to do, then,
notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the Court may, instead of sentencing him to any punishment or releasing him on probation of good conduct under section 4, release him after due admonition.

'Explanation - For the purposes of this section, previous conviction against a person shall include any previous order made against him under this section or section 4'.
33.

A study of above section makes it very clear that a person can be released on probation if he has committed an offence punishable with imprisonment for not more than two years, or with fine, or with both, under the Indian Penal Code, or any other law, and there is no previous conviction proved against him.
34. In the present case, the appellant has been convicted for offence u/s 304 A IPC.

Section 304A IPC reads as under:-
"Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both".
PRAVEEN PRAVEEN KUMAR KUMAR
It is also an undisputed fact that the accused is a first time offender.
36. In the facts and circumstances, it seems to be a perfect case where appellant/accused may be released on probation.

Therefore, keeping in mind the overall facts and circumstances of the case, I find it to be a fit case where appellant needs to be shown some leniency and compassion and,
therefore, I extend benefit of probation to him.

37. Needless to say, the appellant is entitled to benefit u/S 12 of the Probation of Offenders Act which reads as under:-

attaching to a conviction of an offence under such law.

Therefore, instead of sentencing him at once to any punishment, it is directed that he be released on entering into a bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like amount giving undertaking therein to appear and receive sentence when called upon within a period of one year from today and in the meantime, to keep peace and be of good behaviour.

Appellant is directed to furnish the bonds in the trial PRAVEEN PRAVEEN KUMAR KUMAR Date: 2025.03.12 15:25:28 +0530 court.
